accuracy.reason: Every card preserves acceptance/completion, redelivery, ordering and retention limits. Live primary sources support guarantees; both diagrams separate the intended boundaries.

evidence.quote: Neither makes a broker operation atomic with a database write or proves an arbitrary business effect succeeded.

mechanisms.reason: Producer, broker and worker actions lead into commit/ack crash windows and atomic duplicate protection; ordering and overload explain state changes and remedies.

evidence.quote: Commit both or neither. A duplicate ID skips the effect.

coherence.reason: Cards 1-2 establish deferred work and handoff before failure, retries and dependent ordering; capacity and log contrast then inform the synchronous/asynchronous choice.

evidence.quote: Trace publish → broker acceptance → worker effect → consumer acknowledgement.

decisions.reason: All eight objectives combine benefits with user-visible delay, status, duplicate handling, hot-key serialization and finite capacity; card 8 explains when deferral is unsuitable.

evidence.quote: Keep decisions synchronous when the next action requires their result.

clarity.reason: Key terms are defined through actions; the overwrite example explains ordered effects and arithmetic explains backlog without decorative narrative.

evidence.quote: Workers receive them in order, but the slower old update finishes last and overwrites new.

outcomes.reason: C1-C6: learner maps all three actors, confirms handoff before accepted, distinguishes saved file from ack, gives pending/ready/failed visibility, preserves synchronous access decision and names broker/worker/status costs; cards 1,2,8 directly teach these.

C1-C5: learner traces commit-before-ack redelivery and ack-first loss, reuses stable ID, couples unique durable ID and credit in one transaction, and rejects universal exactly-once; card 3 supports every step.

C1-C5: learner delays temporary retries within finite budget, isolates persistent/exhausted failures, exposes failure, keeps healthy work moving and requires cause repair/effect inspection before replay; card 4 teaches all. A numeric budget is not required.

C1-C5: learner derives final 5, separates receive/effect order, serializes per-item including retries, permits other items and states hot-item bottleneck; card 5 gives a transferable overwrite example.

C1-C6: learner computes 40/s, links oldest age to completion delay, bounds saturated downstream concurrency, visibly throttles/rejects admission, recognizes retention/storage/delay bounds and conditions more workers on downstream headroom; card 6 teaches all.

C1-C6: learner distinguishes divided jobs from independent groups, within-group partition sharing and per-group offsets, nondeleting commits, retention-bounded replay, per-partition order and external-effect limits; card 7 explicitly supports all.

sourceChecks.claim: Live Azure asynchronous-request-reply distinguishes accepted processing from later resource availability and status/error observation.
Live RabbitMQ confirms says publisher confirms and consumer acknowledgements are orthogonal; ack permits deletion and unacknowledged deliveries can requeue. Diagram keeps these boundaries distinct.
Live AWS idempotent APIs requires stable caller ID and ACID coordination of token with mutations; RabbitMQ requeue rules support the crash window. No external-effect exactly-once guarantee is made.

Live Azure retry distinguishes transient delay/bounded attempts from canceling persistent faults; Azure queue-based-load-leveling dead-letter guidance supports isolation, diagnosis and deliberate resubmission.

Live Azure competing-consumers warns ordering is not guaranteed and recommends serial group/session handling when needed; concurrent completion can reverse effects, and serial dependency limits throughput.

Live Azure queue-based-load-leveling confirms finite durability/retention, rising latency when producer rate exceeds consumers, bounded aggregate downstream work and producer shedding; arithmetic 100-70=30 checked.

Live Kafka design confirms per-group per-partition offsets, rewind, retention/compaction limits and need to coordinate external effects. Diagram depicts independent consumers without claiming global order.

Live Azure async pattern supports deferral only when result is not required immediately and requires later observable results; synchronous authorization follows the explicit dependency, not a broker guarantee.
